title: Why Detroit: summers hearing the big traveling bands
summary: An aunt in Detroit hosted the boys in summers, where Wilson heard McKinney's Cotton Pickers, Fletcher Henderson, Jimmy Noone and Horace Henderson at the Greystone.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Uh huh. You mentioned that when you left Tuskegee, you went to -- you just mentioned it.
Alabama. Then you went to Detroit -- so how did you get to Detroit? Had you started any music at all? We got to get in to that now.

Well, Detroit came in the picture because I had an aunt and an uncle living in Detroit -- my mother's ... one of her younger sisters who had -- one that was very close to her, one who had helped her in Austin, Texas, when I was born, this sister came out to Austin, Texas to help her with me and my brother so that my mother could go to work and teach. And she was sort of babysitting, taking care of me and my brother.
But when she later married and settled down in

Detroit, my mother used to visit her during our summer vacations in Tuskegee, and take me and my brother there -- and when we'd go to Detroit, I got a chance to hear jazz music, you know, on the high level of the big traveling bands, they would come through.

I remember Jimmy Noone band came over once from Chicago and played at the Greystone Ballroom. I heard regularly McKinney's Cotton Pickers Band every Monday night at the Greystone, and Fletcher Henderson's band came through with Coleman Hawkins and people like that in there -- and Tommy Ladnier, Kaiser Marshall.
Oh, Kaiser -- Kaiser's a Texan, too, you know.
Oh, he is? Kaiser Marshall is from Texas?

So Horace Henderson had a really great band in those days, and Benny Carter, right out of school, want too, in Ohio, they formed this great band, and Rex Steele was in that band -- so I heard this kind of music in my summer vacations in Detroit, and when I go back to Alabama to school, they would -- that impression was just so strong, see. So that was really why Detroit was the town I settled in, and joined the union, tried to start a career after I had left school.
